_meta.source: https://www.mptourism.com/ (official Madhya Pradesh Tourism Board site)
_meta.scope: Madhya Pradesh — expanding the app's existing 10 MP cards with the rest of the state's genuine places of interest
navCategories: Plan Your Trip (Accommodations, Itineraries, Guides, Agents)
_meta.wildlifeHeadline: MP promotes itself as India's 'Tiger State' — 11 National Parks, 24 Wildlife Sanctuaries, 9 Tiger Reserves; also India's first cheetah reintroduction site (Kuno).

destinationsScraped.name: Bhimbetka
destinationsScraped.summary: Prehistoric rock shelters in the forested Vindhyan hills ~45 km SE of Bhopal (Raisen district). 760 shelters, ~500 with rock paintings, the oldest dating back tens of thousands of years (Mesolithic onward; some cupules in the Auditorium Cave far older). UNESCO World Heritage Site (inscribed 2003). Named shelters: Auditorium Rock, Zoo Rock (most densely painted, Mesolithic), Boar Rock, Turtle Rock. Often combined with the nearby Bhojpur Shiva temple (~7.5 ft linga), ~45-50 min away.
destinationsScraped.access: Rail: Bhopal Junction / Obedullaganj (~7 km). Air: Raja Bhoj Airport, Bhopal. Road: ~1-1.5 hr by car from Bhopal via NH46 (Hoshangabad road).
destinationsScraped.notesFromSite: Site page did not give exact timings/fees; ASI site, generally sunrise-sunset, small entry fee.

destinationsScraped.name: Bhedaghat
destinationsScraped.summary: The Marble Rocks gorge on the Narmada near Jabalpur (~20 km): white/cream marble (dolomitic limestone) cliffs rising ~30 m, best seen by boat, and famously on a full-moon night when the marble glows. Dhuandhar ('smoke cascade') Falls where the Narmada plunges in a roaring mist; a ropeway crosses the gorge at the falls. The 10th-century Chausath Yogini temple on a hilltop above the river. 'Bandar Kudni' is the narrowest point. Marble here has been quarried and carved for generations.
destinationsScraped.access: Rail/Air: Jabalpur (~20-25 km). Road: ~30-40 min from Jabalpur.
destinationsScraped.safetyFromSite: In the monsoon the falls thunder at their most powerful; boating in the gorge is suspended when the river is high (monsoon and just after) for safety.

destinationsScraped.name: Omkareshwar
destinationsScraped.summary: Om-shaped island (Mandhata) in the Narmada ~80 km from Indore, Khandwa dist. Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga (1 of 12); linked Mamleshwar temple on the south bank; Gauri Somnath (11th c.), Siddhnath (13th c.), 24 Avatars; island parikrama ~7 km; 270-ft hanging footbridge; Kotitirtha ghat evening aarti; 108-ft Adi Shankaracharya 'Statue of Oneness' installed Sep 2023 (Ekatma Dham). Rail: Omkareshwar Road (Mortakka ~12 km) / Khandwa ~72 km / Indore ~78 km. Air: Indore ~87 km. Best Oct-Mar.

destinationsScraped.name: Maheshwar
destinationsScraped.summary: Narmada-bank town, Khargone dist., ~90 km from Indore, ~40 km from Mandu. 18th-c. capital of Ahilyabai Holkar: Ahilya Fort + Rajwada palace; carved sandstone ghats with chhatris + evening aarti; Baneshwar temple on a river rock; centuries-old handloom centre for the Maheshwari saree (Rehwa Society in the fort). Ahilya Fort heritage hotel + MP Tourism Narmada Retreat. Nearest rail Barwaha ~40 km / Indore. Best Oct-Mar; summer to ~46 C.

destinationsScraped.name: Pench
destinationsScraped.summary: Tiger reserve straddling MP-Maharashtra border (Seoni/Chhindwara dist.), on the Pench river; the 'Jungle Book' country (Seoni hills, Alikatta). Tigers, leopard, dhole, gaur, cheetal, sambar, 280+ birds incl. 4 vulture species. MP-side gates Turia (main), Karmajhiri, Jamtara; buffer night safari. Book via forest.mponline.gov.in. Open ~1 Oct-30 Jun, closed monsoon. Nagpur ~90-130 km (nearest airport/rail); Jabalpur ~200 km.

destinationsScraped.name: Panna
destinationsScraped.summary: Tiger reserve in Vindhya hills (Panna/Chhatarpur dist.), ~25 km from Khajuraho, on the Ken river. Tigers reintroduced from ~2009 after local extinction -- a noted recovery story. Leopard, sloth bear, wild dog, wolf, gharial + mugger croc in the Ken, 7 vulture species, 200+ birds. Gates Madla + Hinauta; Ken boat rides. Pandav Falls (inside park) + Raneh Falls Ken canyon ('Grand Canyon of India') nearby. Open ~Oct-Jun. Entry fee cited: weekday Rs 2450 / weekend Rs 3050. Khajuraho airport + rail ~25 km.

destinationsScraped.name: Kuno National Park
destinationsScraped.summary: National park on the Kuno river in Sheopur dist. (near the MP-Rajasthan border), Sheopur/Shivpuri area. India's cheetah reintroduction site under Project Cheetah: 8 cheetahs from Namibia released 17 Sep 2022, ~12 more from South Africa Feb 2023 -- the cat had been extinct in India since 1952. Dry deciduous forest of kardhai/salai/khair with grasslands; originally prepared as a second home for the Asiatic lion. Also leopard, striped hyena, jackal, sloth bear, chital, sambar, nilgai, chinkara, mugger crocodile, 120+ birds. Limited cheetah safari in the Ahera tourism zone; jeep safaris booked online via forest.mponline.gov.in. Open ~Oct-Jun, closed monsoon. Sightings not guaranteed; the tourism programme is still evolving.
destinationsScraped.access: Air: Gwalior (~170-176 km). Rail: Shivpuri (~65-70 km) or Gwalior. Road: Sesaipura village ~15 km from the park; ~65 km from Shivpuri; ~175 km from Gwalior.
destinationsScraped.safetyNotes: Regulated park -- registered jeep + compulsory forest guide only, no getting out in the forest. Tourism infrastructure new and thin; long transfers from Gwalior/Shivpuri, do road legs by day. Basic local medical facilities (hospitals in Shivpuri/Sheopur). Cheetah-safari zones and rules still evolving and can change/suspend at short notice. Monsoon closure (~Jul-Sep).

destinationsScraped.name: Satpura National Park & Tiger Reserve (Madai/Tawa)
destinationsScraped.summary: Satpura Tiger Reserve in the Satpura hills, Narmadapuram (Hoshangabad) dist., below Pachmarhi; the Denwa river and the Tawa reservoir/dam along its edge, Bori Sanctuary attached. One of the very few Indian reserves allowing walking safaris on foot (guided, single file, forest guard + guide), plus canoe safaris on the Denwa, cycling, boat safaris, jeep drives, buffer night safari. Reached from the Madai (Madhai) gate by crossing the Denwa backwater by boat. Tiger, leopard, sloth bear, wild dog, gaur, sambar, chital, nilgai, Indian giant squirrel, 300+ birds, mugger crocodile on the Denwa. Quieter and wilder-feeling than the big-name parks. Open ~1 Oct-30 Jun, closed monsoon; Oct-Mar best.
destinationsScraped.access: Air: Bhopal (~120-130 km). Rail: Pipariya (~50 km), Itarsi (~70 km, major junction), Narmadapuram (~25 km). Road: Madai is on the Pipariya-Bhopal road; last leg is a boat across the Denwa. Pachmarhi ~100-114 km.
destinationsScraped.safetyNotes: Regulated reserve; every activity runs with a compulsory forest guide (walks also with an armed forest guard) on fixed routes/timings. Walking safaris put you on foot in tiger/leopard/sloth-bear habitat -- single file behind the guard, silence, no straying; sloth bears the main hazard. Canoe/boat safaris on water with muggers -- life jacket, stay seated. Dawn/dusk cold in winter. Permits limited, booked online in advance. Monsoon closure (~Jul-Sep).

destinationsScraped.name: Indore
destinationsScraped.summary: Madhya Pradesh's largest city and commercial capital, on the Malwa plateau. 18th-c. Holkar (Maratha) capital: the seven-storey Rajwada palace facade near Khajuri Bazaar; Lal Bagh Palace (built 1886-1921, ~71 acres, European style); Kanch Mandir (glass-and-mirror Jain temple by Seth Hukumchand); Krishnapura Chhatris (carved sandstone royal cenotaphs on the Khan riverbank); Central Museum (Gupta-to-Parmara sculpture, est. 1929). Temples: Khajrana Ganesh (built by Ahilyabai Holkar, 1735), Bada Ganpati (8 m idol, 1875), Annapurna. Food city: Sarafa Bazaar jewellery market turns into an all-veg night street-food market ~9 pm-1 am; Chhappan Dukan (56 Shops) eating street; signatures poha-jalebi, bhutte ka kees, mawa bati, Indori namkeen. India's cleanest city (Swachh Survekshan) for years running. Base for Mandu/Maheshwar/Omkareshwar/Ujjain.
destinationsScraped.access: Air: Devi Ahilyabai Holkar Airport ~8-10 km W of centre; MP's busiest, links to Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, Ahmedabad etc. Rail: Indore Junction, central; direct trains from Delhi/Mumbai. Road: NH-3 (Agra-Mumbai) x NH-59 (Ahmedabad-Indore); Delhi-Mumbai Expressway; ~3.5h from Bhopal, ~1h Ujjain, ~2h Mandu/Maheshwar. Sarwate + Gangwal bus stands.
destinationsScraped.bestSeason: Oct-Mar (~12-30 C); summers hot to low 40s C.
destinationsScraped.safetyNotes: Regarded as one of central India's more relaxed big cities for women; busy family-oriented public life. Sarafa/Chhappan Dukan stay crowded with families late into the night. Plentiful app cabs/autos, iBus BRT. Normal big-city care: secure valuables in the tight Sarafa/Rajwada crowds, app cabs after dark, empty residential streets late at night. Severe summer heat Apr-Jun.

destinationsScraped.name: Chitrakoot
destinationsScraped.summary: Pilgrimage town on the Mandakini river in the northern Vindhyas, straddling the MP-UP line: the town is in Satna district, MADHYA PRADESH, adjoining Chitrakoot district, Uttar Pradesh, across the river (per district administration / Wikipedia). Tradition places much of the middle of Rama/Sita/Lakshmana's 14-year exile here (~11 of 14 years). Key sites: Ramghat (main ghats on the Mandakini, evening aarti, boats, Diwali Deepdan with 1000+ floated lamps); Kamadgiri (forested hill = Rama, ~5 km barefoot parikrama past temples); Bharat Milap temple; Janki Kund (2 km from Ramghat, Sita's bathing spot); Sphatik Shila (rock with 'footprints' on the left bank); Hanuman Dhara (hilltop/cliff Hanuman temple); Gupt Godavari (cave system ~18 km out, on the UP side, wade through water inside). Busiest on Amavasya (new-moon) days and at Diwali.
destinationsScraped.access: Rail: Chitrakoot Dham Karwi (CKTD) ~8-10 km, on the UP side, links to Delhi/Lucknow/Allahabad/Varanasi/Jhansi; Satna Junction ~75 km (~2h, far more trains, on Mumbai-Howrah line). Air: Prayagraj (Allahabad, Bamrauli) ~106-120 km; Khajuraho ~175-180 km. Road: autos/e-rickshaws/taxis link the scattered sites on both banks; half-day hired auto/taxi covers the circuit.
destinationsScraped.bestSeason: Oct-Mar. Avoid peak summer and the monsoon -- the Mandakini has flooded the ghats and washed out the Ramghat bridge in heavy-rain years (e.g. 2016).
destinationsScraped.accommodationFromSite: MPT Tourist Bungalow (INR 250-2,890), MPT Mandakini Resort (INR 200-2,290), plus many dharamshalas/ashram guesthouses near Ramghat.
destinationsScraped.safetyNotes: Long-established family-oriented pilgrimage town; many women travel, in groups and with elders. Core around Ramghat busy pre-dawn to night aarti. Ordinary pilgrim-town care: valuables in crowds, fix auto/taxi fares, prefer hotel-arranged driver for the full-day circuit. Hanuman Dhara is a steep cliff climb; Kamadgiri parikrama is a long barefoot walk -- daylight only, carry water. Gupt Godavari = wading in a dark cave, go with the crowd. Monsoon flood risk. Don't drink river water.

destinationsScraped.name: Amarkantak
destinationsScraped.summary: Small hilltop pilgrimage town in Anuppur district, far-eastern MP, ~1,000 m, where the Vindhya, Satpura and Maikal ranges meet; forests rich in medicinal plants. Source of the Narmada (at the Narmada Kund + temple complex in town), the Son/Sone (at Sonemuda) and the Johila. Around Narmada Kund: sandstone Kalachuri (Tripuri-Kalachuri era, pre-14th c.) temples -- Machhendranath, Pataleshwar, Kailash Narayan -- and the modern Shri Yantra Mandir (4 goddess heads at the entrance, 64 yoginis). Mai ki Bagiya grove sacred to Narmada (Charanodak Kund). Waterfalls in the forest: Kapildhara (sage Kapila's penance, the most famous) and milky Dugdhdhara ~1 km below, reached by a short trek. Kabir Chabutra (Sant Kabir's meditation site) nearby. Festivals: Narmada Jayanti, Makar Sankranti, Shiv Chaturdashi (winter). Site says 71 km from Anuppur HQ.
destinationsScraped.access: Air: Jabalpur ~228 km, Raipur ~230 km. Rail: Pendra Road (Chhattisgarh) ~42 km; Anuppur ~71 km; Bilaspur bigger junction ~145 km. Road: direct buses from Bilaspur, Katni, Jabalpur, Rewa, Mandla, Seoni, Allahabad, Raipur.
destinationsScraped.bestSeason: Sep-Feb (post-monsoon greenery through cool winter). Hill town -- cold winter mornings/nights.
destinationsScraped.safetyNotes: Small calm pilgrimage town, families/women pilgrims the main visitors; Narmada Kund core busy and lit through evening aarti. Festival-day crowds (Narmada Jayanti, Makar Sankranti) swell the town well beyond normal. Outlying sites (Kapildhara, Dugdhdhara, Sonemuda, Kabir Chabutra) spread through forest -- daylight only, hired auto/jeep via the stay, not alone. Waterfall paths rocky/slick near the water, keep back from edges post-monsoon. Bottled/filtered water only.

destinationsScraped.name: Chanderi
destinationsScraped.summary: Historic small town in Ashoknagar district, between the Malwa plateau and Bundelkhand; ~103 km from Jhansi, ~214 km from Bhopal. Famous for the Chanderi saree -- sheer lightweight handloom of silk-cotton / Chanderi cotton / pure silk with gold-silver zari (coin, flower, peacock motifs); ~5,000 looms, 9,000+ weavers (2017). Monuments: Chanderi Fort (Kirti Durg, 11th c. by Kirti Pal; three gates incl. Khooni Darwaza); Koshak Mahal (1445, Sultan Mahmud Shah Khilji of Malwa); Badal Mahal gate (~1450, >15 m); Jama Masjid (believed 13th c., the only Jama Masjid in India without minars); Shehzadi ka Rauza (15th c., princess Mehrunnisa); Battisi Baoli (stepwell, 1485, 32 steps); Khandargiri (Jain site, 45-ft Adinatha). History: Malwa Sultanate, Bundela Rajputs, Mughals; Medini Rai's last stand vs Babur, 1528. Film locations: Sui Dhaaga, Stree.
destinationsScraped.access: Air: Gwalior ~214-230 km, Bhopal ~215 km. Rail: Lalitpur ~37-40 km (Delhi-Bhopal main line, ~1h by road), Ashoknagar ~46-50 km, Mungaoli. Road: from Lalitpur, Jhansi, Ashoknagar, Bhopal, Indore, Ujjain.
destinationsScraped.safetyNotes: Quiet low-key heritage town, small-scale tourism; monuments among residential lanes that empty after dark -- sightsee by day. Fort, old ramps and historic stepwells (Battisi Baoli etc.) have steep steps and unfenced drops. Hired auto/taxi via the hotel for the fort top and Khandargiri. Public transport thins in the evening; arrive/leave via Lalitpur by daylight. Hot, largely unshaded fort -- water + hat.

destinationsScraped.name: Jabalpur
destinationsScraped.summary: Largest city of the Mahakoshal region, in a rocky basin ~10 km N of the Narmada. Chief role: base for Bhedaghat (~25-27 km) -- the Marble Rocks gorge + Dhuandhar Falls (~98 ft). City sights: Madan Mahal Fort (Gond dynasty, 12th c./1116 CE, on a granite outcrop ~500 m); Balancing Rock (boulder poised on a narrow base, rode out a 6.5-magnitude quake); Chausath Yogini temple (10th c., at Bhedaghat, one of India's largest yogini temples, ~41 m circumference); Rani Durgavati Museum (Kalachuri sculpture); Tilwara Ghat (Gandhi's ashes immersed); Pisanhari ki Madiya (~500-yr Jain centre); Dumna Nature Reserve (1,058 ha); Bargi Dam ~40 km (45-min cruises). Rail/road/air hub for Kanha, Bandhavgarh, Pench.
destinationsScraped.access: Air: Dumna Airport ~20 km -- Mumbai, Delhi, Pune, Nagpur, Bhopal, Indore; closest airport to Kanha/Bandhavgarh. Rail: Jabalpur Junction, West Central Railway hub, wide connectivity. Road: on NH44/NH34; ~25 km Bhedaghat, ~160 km Bandhavgarh, ~170 km Kanha, ~300 km Bhopal.
destinationsScraped.bestSeason: Oct-Mar for the city; Jul-Sep for fullest waterfalls at Bhedaghat (site pushes the monsoon).
destinationsScraped.safetyNotes: Large university/cantonment city; Civil Lines & Wright Town lit and active in the evening; app cabs/autos plentiful. Bhedaghat: keep back from the unfenced wet-marble ledges above Dhuandhar Falls; gorge boating suspended when the Narmada runs high (monsoon + just after). BOAT SAFETY: a cruise boat capsized on the Bargi Dam reservoir on 30 April 2026 (Jabalpur cruise tragedy / 'Narmada Queen'), 13 of 31 aboard died, sudden strong winds/rough water, life jackets were in sealed storage and inaccessible; CM ordered a high-level inquiry, staff terminated, MPT Marble Rocks Resort manager suspended (verified via news + Wikipedia 'Jabalpur cruise tragedy'). Advice in card: only board a boat that isn't overloaded, put on an accessible life jacket before departure, don't go out in rough/windy weather.
destinationsScraped.fixesDanglingRef: Bhedaghat card (mp_batch1) already links nearbyPlaces id 'jabalpur' -- now resolved.

destinationsScraped.name: Burhanpur
destinationsScraped.summary: Historic town on the Tapti (Tapi) river in the Nimar region of southern MP, near the Maharashtra border. Founded ~1400 as the Faruqi dynasty capital; later a key Mughal city and Deccan military base ('gateway to southern India'). Monuments: Shahi Qila (royal fort-palace on the Tapti, Persian-painted hammam/ceiling; Mumtaz Mahal's body first lay here after she died at Burhanpur in 1631, before its move to Agra); Ahukhana (hunting enclosure garden = her first burial place); Jama Masjid (1589, completed under Akbar, intricate arches, said to be minaret-less per some sources though photos show a minaret); Asirgarh Fort (~20 km, vast hill fort, ancient Shiva temple); Kundi Bhandara (~400-yr-old underground water-filtration/tunnel system, still functioning); Raja Jai Singh observatory; Black Taj / Shah Nawaz Khan tomb; Dargah-e-Hakimi (Dawoodi Bohra pilgrimage, garden bungalows); Gurudwara Badi Sangat (Sikh, historic Guru visit). Food: Burhanpuri jalebi, Mughlai kebabs/korma, khopra pak, mawa jalebi.
destinationsScraped.access: Rail: Burhanpur station on the Delhi-Mumbai main line via Bhusaval -- frequent expresses, easiest way in; ~7-8h from Mumbai. Air: Indore ~180 km (nearest). Road: ~20 km Asirgarh, ~90 km Jalgaon, ~180 km Indore; buses from Indore, Khandwa, Jalgaon.
destinationsScraped.bestSeason: Oct-Mar; summers very hot in the Tapti valley.
destinationsScraped.safetyNotes: Settled ordinary town, low-key tourism, monuments within everyday neighbourhoods -- sightsee by day. Parts of Shahi Qila unrestored: loose steps, low doorways, unlit passages (carry a torch). Asirgarh Fort is a big, hot, largely unshaded hilltop with steep uneven stretches and unfenced drops -- go early, carry water, don't wander far ramparts alone; hire a known taxi via the hotel for Asirgarh + Kundi Bhandara. Modest dress for mosques/dargah/gurudwara (head covering at the last two). Time train arrivals/departures for daylight.

destinationsScraped.name: Maihar
destinationsScraped.summary: Temple town in the Satna region of eastern MP (now the seat of its own Maihar district), on the Mumbai-Howrah main line ~40 km from Satna. Focus: Maa Sharda Devi temple on Trikuta hill -- ~1,063 steps or a ropeway; counted among the Shakti Peethas (Sati's necklace fell here); Alha-Udal akhara at the base (folk-epic warriors' practice ground). Also the home of the Maihar gharana of Hindustani music -- Ustad Allauddin Khan settled here, taught from 1918 (Ravi Shankar, Ali Akbar Khan); Allauddin Khan Sangeet Academy. Other sites: Golamath Shiva temple (10th-11th c.), Maihar fort (Bundela), Bansagar dam ~25 km. Busiest by far during Navratri (twice a year).
destinationsScraped.access: Rail: Maihar station, regular expresses Delhi/Bhopal/Kolkata/Varanasi/Mumbai -- simplest way in. Air: Jabalpur ~160 km, Khajuraho ~140 km. Road: NH-34 from Satna (~40 km), Rewa, Jabalpur, Chitrakoot.
destinationsScraped.bestSeason: Oct-Mar; avoid peak Navratri days for a calmer visit.
destinationsScraped.safetyNotes: Long-established pilgrimage town, women/families/temple groups the majority. Step path + ropeway busy and staffed with police/volunteer queue management in season. MAIN RISK: crowd crush on the narrow stepped hill path during Navratri -- avoid peak days if possible, follow police queue system, don't push, keep children close, use the ropeway to skip the stair crush. The ~1,063-step climb is strenuous and largely unshaded (water, pace, ropeway for heart/mobility concerns). Rooms vanish around Navratri -- book ahead or base in Satna. Sealed water + freshly cooked food. No specific stampede incident found in searches -- advice is standard hilltop-shrine prudence, not a reported event.

destinationsScraped.name: Datia
destinationsScraped.summary: Small town in northern MP near Jhansi, on the Delhi-Chennai railway. Bir Singh Deo Palace (Satkhanda / Purana Mahal): ~7-storey brick-and-stone palace raised by Bundela ruler Raja Bir Singh Deo ~1620, by tradition never inhabited; built without wood or iron; stacked arches, chhatris, oriel windows, central tower, surviving Bundela murals inside. Peetambara Peeth at the town edge -- among India's most-visited Shakti temples; complex also holds rare Dhumavati Devi and Bagulamukhi temples and the ancient Vankhandeshwar Shiva shrine. Unao-Balaji Sun temple nearby. Called 'Laghu Vrindavan'; Mahabharata reference as 'Daityavakra'. Fills during Navratri.
destinationsScraped.access: Rail: Datia station on the Delhi-Jhansi-Chennai line (some Vande Bharat/expresses stop); Jhansi ~28 km (major junction, far more trains, ~30 min). Air: Gwalior ~75-90 km (practical); small Datia airstrip with occasional Bhopal/Khajuraho flights; Jhansi ~25 km. Road: ~28 km Jhansi, ~75 km Gwalior, just off NH44; easy loop with Jhansi + Orchha.
destinationsScraped.safetyNotes: Small ordinary town, heavy but orderly pilgrim flow to Peetambara Peeth (well-staffed). Bir Singh Deo Palace = ASI site, seven levels of open terraces/parapets and dim internal staircases with unfenced drops and uneven treads -- daylight only, torch, keep away from edges, children in hand. Peetambara Peeth very busy on Navratri and Saturdays -- follow queue management, mind valuables, long waits. Sightsee in daylight; use autos for short hops; most travellers base in Orchha/Jhansi and day-trip. Unshaded palace -- carry water.

destinationsScraped.name: Bhojpur
destinationsScraped.url: https://www.mptourism.com/destination-bhojpur.php (404 at time of scrape -- primary sources used: Wikipedia 'Bhojeshwar Temple' + raisen.nic.in tourist-place page)
destinationsScraped.summary: Small village on the Betwa in Raisen district, ~28 km SE of Bhopal, named for Paramara king Bhoja (r. c.1010-1055) who began but never finished the Bhojeshwar Temple on a rock terrace here. Temple raised to sanctum height and roofed with a flat slab; spire never built. Works frozen mid-construction: unfinished blocks, masons' setting-out marks, full-size architectural drawings incised on surrounding rock, and a ~90 m (300 ft) earthen-and-stone haulage ramp. Inside: four huge octagonal pillars (~12 m) framing one of India's largest Shiva lingas -- single stone ~2.3 m (7.5 ft) tall, ~5.4 m (17.8 ft) circumference, on a composite platform lifting the whole to >12 m (platform ~6.5 m/21.5 ft per side). Nearby: Jain shrine with a tall Shantinatha image; traces of Paramara-era dams that held a large lake across the Betwa (18.5 x 7.5 miles per Wikipedia), breached in the 15th c. (traditionally attributed to Hoshang Shah of Malwa). ASI Monument of National Importance; on India's UNESCO tentative list.
destinationsScraped.access: Air: Raja Bhoj Airport, Bhopal ~35 km. Rail: Obaidullaganj ~7 km (Bhopal-Itarsi line); most drive from Bhopal. Road: ~28 km (~1h) from Bhopal via the Hoshangabad road; ~30 km from Bhimbetka. Best as a half-day taxi from Bhopal combined with Bhimbetka + the Bhojpur Jain temple.
destinationsScraped.bestSeason: Oct-Mar; monsoon greenery but the rock terrace gets slippery.
destinationsScraped.safetyNotes: Compact ticketed ASI monument (sunrise-sunset, small fee), caretaker present, also a working local temple. No accommodation or real infrastructure -- half-day trip from Bhopal, don't get stranded after dark (no transport). Open rock terrace with unfinished blocks, the old ramp, uneven unfenced edges -- watch footing, worse after rain. Carry own water + sun cover, minimal shade, only a couple of stalls. Arrange the taxi via a Bhopal hotel/known operator and agree the Bhimbetka-circuit fare up front.
destinationsScraped.linga_measurement_note: MP Tourism-adjacent sources and Wikipedia give the linga as ~2.3 m / 7.5 ft tall (some popular sources say ~5.5 m -- that figure appears to conflate linga + platform, which together exceed 12 m). Card uses the sourced ~2.3 m linga on a platform bringing the whole to >12 m.

destinationsScraped.name: Shivpuri
destinationsScraped.summary: District town in northern MP among wooded Vindhyan hills on the old Agra-Bombay road; came under the Scindias of Gwalior in 1804, became a favoured retreat. The Chhatris: walled ensemble of white-marble cenotaphs to Madho Rao Scindia and his mother Maharani Sakhya Raje -- Hindu shikharas + Mughal domes + pietra-dura inlay, in a formal charbagh garden with tanks and a small Shiva temple. Madhav National Park: 355 sq km dry forest + grassland around Sakhya Sagar and Madhav (Chandpatha) lakes; chital, sambar, nilgai, chinkara, blackbuck, leopard, sloth bear, tigers reintroduced in recent years; George Castle (crenellated hilltop shooting lodge built by Maharaja Jivaji Rao Scindia for a 1911/George V-era royal visit that never happened, now a small museum). Madhav Vilas Palace (Scindia summer palace, run as a heritage hotel). Bhadaiya Kund, Bhura Khon springs (not on the MP Tourism page; from other sources).
destinationsScraped.access: Air: Gwalior ~110-130 km. Rail: Shivpuri station (limited services); Gwalior ~110-120 km / Jhansi ~97-100 km are the big junctions. Road: on NH44 (Delhi-Bengaluru corridor); ~110-120 km (~2.5h) from Gwalior, ~100 km from Jhansi, ~230 km from Bhopal; frequent buses from Gwalior, Jhansi, Guna.
destinationsScraped.bestSeason: Nov-Mar (winter); Madhav National Park closed in the monsoon (~Jul-Sep).
destinationsScraped.safetyNotes: Settled district town, ordinary public life, small tourist circuit (Chhatris, palace, park), on NH44 with frequent buses. Chhatris + Madhav Vilas Palace are ticketed staffed sites; MP Tourism runs lakeside accommodation. Madhav NP is leopard/sloth-bear/(recently) tiger habitat -- take park permission, keep to the designated route, stay in the vehicle, permitted times + guide where required. George Castle and lakeside points are quiet, lightly visited -- daylight, not entirely alone. Town market fine in the evening; outer/park-approach roads unlit -- taxi. Cold winter park mornings.
